clue.text: On the continent, I experienced war

parts.note: je is the French for I, French being a language of the continent
had, as in had a bad time, means experienced

explanation.surface: A veteran recalls fighting in a war somewhere in mainland Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the continent' tells you to translate 'I' into French. The Times of the day spelt this holy war JEHAD; JIHAD is the commoner form now.
explanation.definitionFit: A jehad is a holy war waged by Muslims, so the general word for armed conflict covers it.

clue.text: Sailor on boat -he used to work with ropes

definitions.text: he used to work with ropes

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the sailor sits on top of the boat

parts.note: jack, as in jack tar, is a sailor
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A seaman aboard ship worked with ropes all day.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Ketch was a notorious 17th-century English executioner, and his name became slang for the hangman. The ropes are nooses, not rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Ketch was a byword for the public hangman, whose trade was the noose.

clue.text: Poet in the right

parts.note: at home, someone is in

explanation.surface: A poet is morally correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' means at home, as in 'is she in?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer is the ancient Greek bard credited with the Iliad and Odyssey.

clue.text: Transferring 500 servicemen can put end to training

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
the RAF, Royal Air Force, is a British armed service
a tin is a can

indicators.note: end to picks out the closing letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Moving 500 troops can complete their instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb; it is TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Drafting means sending or detailing people from one place to another, as soldiers are moved.

clue.text: Chastise wanton whores with it

indicators.note: wanton means unruly and undisciplined, so the letters of the word beside it run wild

parts.note: hip means fashionable, as does with it

explanation.surface: A moralist urges punishment for loose women and the use of a whip on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanton' rearranges WHORES to give HORSEW, and HIP is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To horsewhip someone is to beat them with a riding whip, a harsh way to punish.

clue.text: Gangster pursued by a sheriff

explanation.definitionFit: A hood is a hoodlum or thug; Robin Hood was the outlaw chased by the Sheriff of Nottingham.

clue.text: Riotous gathering, about 50, represents a quarter of the revolution

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anagram goes round the numeral
riotous means wild and out of order, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A rowdy meeting of fifty or so stands for part of the uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riotous' rearranges GATHERING into RIGHTANGE, and 'about' puts it round L. 'revolution' suggests uprising but means a full turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A full turn is 360 degrees and a right angle is 90, one fourth of it.

clue.text: Foreign money subscribed to Royal Commission

indicators.note: subscribed means written underneath, so in a down entry the money comes below

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher
the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: Overseas cash is donated to a royal inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal Commission' reads as a phrase, but the definition is 'Commission' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission is a task one is sent to do, as an errand is.

clue.text: Pack horse used around States

indicators.note: around tells us the horse surrounds the verb

parts.note: a hack is a horse for ordinary riding
avers means states or asserts

explanation.surface: A pack horse is used across America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' suggests the USA but is the verb AVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A haversack is a bag carried on the back, a kind of knapsack.

clue.text: Flourishing ancient city, abandoned by ancient god

indicators.note: abandoned by means left, so the god's name is taken away from the city

parts.note: Palmyra was an ancient city in Syria
Ra was the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A thriving old city is deserted by a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: PALMYRA loses RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmy days are prosperous ones, from the palm as a sign of triumph.

clue.text: Hurry up and move forward

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both an urging to be quick and an idiom for making progress, as a project does when it advances.

clue.text: Festival's prize sent back

indicators.note: something sent back goes the other way, so the word for the prize is read from its end

parts.note: to prize something open is to lever it

explanation.surface: An award at a festival is returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prize' is a verb here: to prize or lever a lid open. The 's after Festival stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A revel is a lively celebration, the kind of merrymaking held at a festival.

clue.text: Ms Greenaway involves gunmen in fighting

indicators.note: involves means wraps up, so the name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Kate Greenaway was a Victorian illustrator of children's books
the RA, the Royal Artillery, is the British army's gunnery regiment

explanation.surface: A woman named Greenaway drags armed men into a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gunmen' suggests gangsters, but in crosswords it is the British army's gunnery regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese martial art of unarmed combat with strikes and kicks.

clue.text: Fish and insects turn a drab colour

indicators.note: turn means go about, so the word for the insects is read backwards

parts.note: nits are the eggs or young of lice, small insects
gray (also spelt grey) is a dull colour

explanation.surface: Fish and bugs fade to a dull hue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses only the insects, giving STIN. 'Fish and insects' looks like a list of creatures; only 'Fish' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The stingray is a flat sea creature with a venomous barbed tail, one kind of fish.

clue.text: I'm in prison without money, that's the snag

indicators.note: without means outside, so the confinement surrounds the money

parts.note: pent means shut in, as one is in prison
a dime is a US coin

explanation.surface: A jailed debtor complains that being penniless is the problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking, and 'in prison' as one phrase means penned up.
explanation.definitionFit: An impediment is an obstacle or hitch.

clue.text: What you would call us in explosive context

clue.text: Aid US pays out — it provides reassurance

indicators.note: out means not in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: American aid is paid away as a comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges AID US PAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is said to comfort a child who has fallen or is being lifted.

clue.text: Try to sell a bird

explanation.definitionFit: Street traders hawk goods by crying them out for sale; the bird is a hunting raptor such as the sparrowhawk.

clue.text: Horatio Herbert Christopher-a name to shout about

parts.note: Kit is a short form of Christopher

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shout goes round the letter

parts.note: to cheer is to shout

explanation.surface: Someone with three first names is worth applauding.
explanation.walkthrough: Horatio Herbert were the first names of Lord Kitchener, the British field marshal of First World War recruiting posters.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Herbert were the given names of Earl Kitchener, the soldier.

clue.text: A clue, in the main, for time

annotationWithheld.why: A clue, in the main, for time (8): the definition is time, but no parse of 'A clue, in the main' gives MIDNIGHT, and a search found no source for it.
annotationWithheld.clue: A clue, in the main, for time

clue.text: Prophet deprived of a pipe

indicators.note: deprived of means losing, so the named letter is taken from the prophet's name

parts.note: Hosea is a prophet with a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A holy man loses his smoking pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deprived of a' takes A from HOSEA. 'pipe' wants to be tobacco; it is a flexible tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A hose is a flexible tube for carrying water, a kind of pipe.

clue.text: One who provides a luncheon voucher

explanation.definitionFit: Slang names a person you rely on for money a meal ticket; literally it is a coupon exchanged for food.

clue.text: On reflection, a sap holds the key to the puzzle

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so everything that follows is read backwards
holds means contains, so the sap word goes round the key

parts.note: to sap a wall is to mine under it
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, a fool has the solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sap' looks like a fool but is the verb to undermine, MINE. A plus MGINE (G inside MINE) reads AMGINE, and 'On reflection' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a riddle or mystery.

clue.text: Movingly depict an academic

indicators.note: movingly suggests letters on the move, shifted to new places

explanation.surface: Describe a scholar in touching terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movingly' looks like a description of the portrait; it rearranges DEPICT AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantic means fussily scholarly, overly concerned with fine points of learning.

clue.text: College beginning to prepare for growth

parts.note: poly, short for polytechnic, was a kind of British college

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of the word after

explanation.surface: A college starts readying itself for expansion.
explanation.walkthrough: POLY is a polytechnic, a type of British higher-education college.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyp is a small growth on a membrane, as in the nose.

clue.text: Kidnap and return Brown's child

indicators.note: return means come back, so the colour with its s is read backwards

parts.note: tan is a brown colour; with the 's it gives tans

explanation.surface: Abduct someone, then hand back the Browns' little one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses the colour with its possessive s, giving SNAT. 'Kidnap and return' reads as a crime in two steps; only 'Kidnap' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To snatch a person is to seize and carry them off, a synonym for abduct.

clue.text: It's worshipped in Shinto temples

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something is revered in Japanese temples.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across SHINTO TEMPLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or creature revered as a sacred emblem.

clue.text: Disparage the rise of Australian football, displacing English

annotationWithheld.why: Disparage the rise of Australian football, displacing English (4): the parse is RULES (Aussie Rules) reversed with E (English) removed, but the stored tree drops the clue word on E and the check then reads 'displacing' as a move, so it is refused.
annotationWithheld.clue: Disparage the rise of Australian football, displacing English

clue.text: Prone to deception

explanation.definitionFit: Lying means stretched out flat, face down; it also means telling untruths, the act of deceiving.

clue.text: Instruct unmarried people to lose weight

parts.note: people are men, and taking away M, the abbreviation for married, leaves EN
to lighten is to become less heavy

explanation.surface: An order is issued for single folk to slim down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unmarried people' works as MEN with M (the abbreviation for married) removed. 'unmarried' suggests singles, but the un- strips a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlighten someone is to give them knowledge, to teach or inform them.

clue.text: Same party can provide the one who holds the purse strings

definitions.text: the one who holds the purse strings

indicators.note: can provide says the letters of these words may be made into something else

explanation.surface: Every political party offers a treasurer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can provide' rearranges SAME PARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A paymaster pays out wages and controls spending, so he controls the money.

clue.text: Watch, for instance, when terms of reference are rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for the terms is reversed

parts.note: a remit is the scope of a body's task, its terms of reference

explanation.surface: A committee's brief is thrown out and someone keeps an eye on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are rejected' reverses REMIT. 'Watch' is a noun here, a timepiece, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A timer is a device for measuring time, as a wristwatch or stopwatch is.
